After two years of silence, according to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple is developing a brand-new iMac equipped with the M6 chip and new colour options, expected to launch before the end of the year.

The iMac has never been updated frequently, having skipped both the M2 and M5 series chips, and still does not offer a larger-screen version — Apple has instead steered high-end users toward the Mac Studio or Mac mini paired with a Studio Display. Despite this, Apple is still preparing to launch a new model equipped with the M6 chip.

Gurman pointed out that this update will include "some new colour options," but did not mention specific modifications. When Apple updated the M4 version in 2024, the colour tones were slightly adjusted, but the actual 7 colour options remained unchanged, with only minor differences in shade. The iMac is also expected to launch before the end of the year:

This means that this autumn will be a fairly important season for the Mac. The product line includes: a fully revamped MacBook Pro with a touchscreen and Tandem OLED, a new entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro equipped with the M6, new Mac Studio models with M5 Max and M5 Ultra (subject to availability), and a new iMac equipped with the M6. Another possibility is a new version of the Mac mini equipped with the M6 and M5 Pro, though it is expected to launch a little later.

Apple's M6 chip will be the first Mac chip to use the new 2nm process, but according to reports there will be no M6 Pro, M6 Max or M6 Ultra versions — instead, the company will accelerate the rollout of the M7 series.
